GLOBAL.EldritchSovereignLoreConcept.description: Wizards banished to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Astral Void[/hyperlink] must endure the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept]Torment of Shadows[/hyperlink]. Those that fail the trial lose themselves to madness and become [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept]Lost Wizards[/hyperlink]. Some of these unfortunate souls, however, continue to grow their power until they regain a twisted fraction of sanity as Eldritch Sovereigns. Mangled, shattered, and deconstructed, their powers allow them to pierce the planar veils, unleashing their corrupting ambitions on the worlds. One of their most fearsome talents is their ability to enthrall not just creatures such as [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept]Astral Sea Monsters[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept]Umbral Demons[/hyperlink], but even entire races to their will.

GLOBAL.ElyaLoreConcept.name: Elya
GLOBAL.ElyaLoreConcept.description: Elya is a young [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept]Maer[/hyperlink], a mystical species of benevolent [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept]Astral Sea Creatures[/hyperlink]. Unlike many others of her people, Elya feels a strong connection to mortals and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink] the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. Her youth and curiosity bring her closer to [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] - and danger - than any other of her kind would dare.

GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept.name: Endailon
GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept.description:
The Endailon are powerful cosmic entities from ancient times. They appear to be heavily linked to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinitiesLoreConcept]Magic Affinities[/hyperlink], to the point that some [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] believe that the magic of the cosmos is a manifestation of the Endailon rather than the Endailon being mere manifestations of the affinities themselves.

Emerging myths surround the Endailon, depicting them as the original gods alongside the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink] who shaped the cosmos and ruled the races throughout. But there is little evidence of the Endailon's motivations and whether or not they concern themselves with the affairs of mortals. In ages past, the Endailon [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept]clashed with the Archons[/hyperlink], leading to their imprisonment within [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept]Grexolis[/hyperlink]. Now, with the opening of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept]Grexolis[/hyperlink], they roam freely again and will leave their mark on the cosmos once more.

GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept.name: Endailon Crisis
GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept.description: Little is known about the Endailon Crisis, though it has become a topic of great interest among the scholars of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink]. What has been established as commonly accepted knowledge, is that the Endailon Crisis happened in a distant age, before the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurielLoreConcept]first Godir[/hyperlink] set foot on [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink]. It was a conflict of cosmic scale, involving the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept]Endailon[/hyperlink] and possibly factions under their influence on one side, and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and their allies—notably among them the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AncientKrazuraLoreConcept]Ancient Krazura[/hyperlink]—on the other. The Endailon Crisis ended with the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept]Endailon[/hyperlink] becoming locked within [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept]Grexolis[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept.name: Eternal Council
GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept.description:
Originally, the Eternal Council was founded as a council of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink], where the matters of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink] and the many [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink] which it spanned would be discussed under the honorary leadership of the Titans. Later, when the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept]Traitor Kings[/hyperlink] had revoked any allegiance to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink], only the wisest of the Giant Kings remained in the Eternal Council. They moved the seat of the council away from Titan’s Henge and indeed their discussions focused less and less on the government of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink], but instead on the mysteries of the cosmos.

In scholarly union, the Eternal Council explored the various applications of crystal magic, seeking to employ Lithorite to immortalize their knowledge—and at last themselves. As their opus magnum, the Eternal Council transferred their souls into Lithorite crystals, escaping Archon judgment and becoming the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept]Eternal Sages[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept.name: Eternal Sages
GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept.description:
Once the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept]wisest Giant Kings[/hyperlink] of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink], the Eternal Sages have left behind their mortal bodies, transferring their souls into Lithorite crystals. They are wielders of powerful crystal magic, commanding the Lithorine and blessing their followers with large stature and crystalline resilience.

The Eternal Sages no longer concern themselves much with the matters of mortals. Instead, all their actions are directed towards the collection and preservation of knowledge, which they store in vast crystal libraries of their own making. It is said that the Eternal Sages know the answer to every enigma the cosmos holds, yet persuading them to share any such knowledge can be a task for eternity.

GLOBAL.FireClanLoreConcept.name: Fire Clan
GLOBAL.FireClanLoreConcept.description: The most aggressive of the Giant Clans, the Fire Clan often seeks direct confrontation with the Rulers of a realm. Claiming distant heritage of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink], these Giants like to unleash terrible war beasts and wage war on the people settling in the lands they regard as their own.

GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept.name: Fracture
GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept.description:
Fractures are tears in the very fabric of magic, altering any spell cast near them. They were the byproduct of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept]Unmakers[/hyperlink]' experiments and often appear around their ruins and magical wastes. Exposure to these fractures, or to the inward winds they produce, can mutate both mana and life itself.

Fractures grow unstable and increase in size as they swallow and twist magic, to a point where they can explode; scattering Astral Barrens, contaminating the area, and creating new fractures. A great number of unstable Fractures in a realm can cause a massive calamity, such as the cataclysm known as [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept]the Fracturing[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.GeassadaeLoreConcept.name: Geassadae
GLOBAL.GeassadaeLoreConcept.description:
As the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathadaeLoreConcept]Duathadae[/hyperlink] and their Mistwalker servants became a greater threat to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink], the general interest in the Fey realm [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept]Duatha[/hyperlink] was rekindled, since old lore might expose the Duathadae's unknown weaknesses. The search through ancient scriptures and chronicles revealed that once a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CircleOfDeogaiLoreConcept]Circle of Deogai[/hyperlink] had existed on [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept]Duatha[/hyperlink], and—more importantly—that the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathadaeLoreConcept]Duathadae[/hyperlink] may not be the only lords of the Fey.

Myths about the Geassadae were uncovered, powerful Fey who may have once ruled [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept]Duatha[/hyperlink], before falling victim to the Duathadae's dark enchantments. Though it has been warned that such tales may only be a perfidious variant of Fey trickery themselves.

GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept.name: Giants
GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept.description:
A relatively rare but imposing sight to behold, giants once roamed the primordial [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink] in greater numbers. In the early days of the cosmos, giants directed the flow of the land and shaped the continents upon each world. This purportedly piqued the ire of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Dragons[/hyperlink] who had formed worlds in a certain way before the giants and were unimpressed with their later adjustments.

True giants tend to come in various forms, usually associated with an element that they have a certain amount of control over. A number of offshoot races of Giantkin and other subtypes have also come into being over the ages through various intermingling of races.

GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept.name: Giant King
GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept.description: Sometimes Elder Giants, sometimes Giants of younger ages blessed with immense power and size, the Giant Kings trace their regal claim on the realms back to the Giant kingdom of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink]. Masters of the forge and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]shapers of worlds[/hyperlink], the Giant Kings are primal forces to be reckoned with. Gladly they will tell tales about the days of the Great Hunt, when Elder Giants tamed the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrwildernessLoreConcept]Urwilderness[/hyperlink] and slew its Primordial Beasts.

GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept.name: Gloomwatch
GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept.description: The Gloomwatch is a diverse faction, incorporating many different races and cultures. They are united by their worship of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinitiesLoreConcept]Affinities[/hyperlink] and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DreamersLoreConcept]Dreamers[/hyperlink] and their eternal fight against the forces of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink]. Their alleged history dates back to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and their first leader Irith of the Scrying Fountain, chronicling a mythic tale of how the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept]Maer[/hyperlink] and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SyronLoreConcept]Syrons[/hyperlink] descended from these celestial origins.

GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept.name: Godir
GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept.description: The Wizards of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept]Pantheon[/hyperlink] who gather at [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink] are called Godir. From there they seek new knowledge and journey to new realms in the Astral Sea. Some of the Godir are newly [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AscendedChampLoreConcept]Ascended Champions[/hyperlink]—while others are ancient [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept]Wizard Kings[/hyperlink] or [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Elder Dragons[/hyperlink], seeking dominion over new realms and people through their mastery of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinitiesLoreConcept]Affinities[/hyperlink]. Godir have achieved a form of immortality: if they are vanquished, they are cast into the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Astral Void[/hyperlink] and seek to rematerialize in Magehaven.

GLOBAL.GreatUmbralWarLoreConcept.name: Great Umbral War
GLOBAL.GreatUmbralWarLoreConcept.description:
The Great Umbral War broke out when [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LithylLoreConcept]Lithyl Nightweaver[/hyperlink] launched an invasion on [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AthlaLoreConcept]Athla[/hyperlink], unleashing the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept]swarming hordes[/hyperlink] of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink] from the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept]Umbral Abyss[/hyperlink]. Yet it was only the beginning, for soon thereafter [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EldritchSovereignLoreConcept]Eldritch Sovereigns[/hyperlink] all across the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink] began similar assaults, enshrouding the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink] with their corruptive gloom.

Though the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink] attained the aid of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept]Gloomwatch[/hyperlink] and later the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink], the enemy is tenacious and its maddening reach can corrupt even Godir. Therefore much hope is placed in the powers of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept]Endailon[/hyperlink], despite their unfathomable influence and motives.

GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept.name: Grexolis
GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept.description: A fractured [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]World[/hyperlink] hidden in the mists of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. The [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] left a custodian to guard the secrets which lie buried here.

GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept.name: Horwynd
GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept.description:
When the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AncientKrazuraLoreConcept]Ancient Krazura[/hyperlink] became locked in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept]Grexolis[/hyperlink], their distant relatives, the Horwynd, took it upon themselves to preserve their knowledge and memory. They fled from the sphere of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archon[/hyperlink] influence and no chronicles speak of their destination or fate.

And yet they returned ages later, revealing the Shrouded Isles they created through unbreakable pacts with the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept]Wizard Kings[/hyperlink]. With pride they eulogize their Tree of Wisdom and its schools of magic. But their homeland and its history remain a mortal secret.

GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept.name: Lost Wizard
GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept.description:
A Lost Wizard was once a powerful wizard who, either by foolhardy choice or forced exile, found themselves in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Astral Void[/hyperlink] and succumbed to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept]Torment of Shadows[/hyperlink]. These power-hungry husks now glide with deadly purpose through the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink] as one of the myriad [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept]Monsters[/hyperlink] that roam its depths, preying upon the unwary.

While it retains an affinity for magic and even clutches its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept]Tome of Spells[/hyperlink] greedily, its physical form has twisted to match its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]environment[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept.name: Maer
GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept.description:
The Maer are a rare breed of sentient merfolk, residing deep within the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. Where mortals find travel through the Astral Sea tedious and dangerous, these beings move through it with ease and grace, singing along to songs no one else can hear.

The Maer are such a rare sight that many schooled mortals deem their existence a myth, a story of solace to explain the strange sounds heard during the travels through the Astral Sea. But these benevolent, solitary creatures of magic and song are as real as the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept]horrors[/hyperlink] that plague the currents.

GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept.name: Magehaven
GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept.description:
Magehaven is a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]World[/hyperlink] in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink] where the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept]Pantheon[/hyperlink] of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] hold their most important forum of dispute and council. It is protected by an unbreakable spell which prevents any harm from being done to a living creature or [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept]Soul[/hyperlink]. Therefore, even the fiercest enemies can meet there to negotiate their conflicts.

Magehaven is located close to [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept]the Well[/hyperlink] and bears remnants of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] who once dwelt there. Among the many wonders of Magehaven are the Library of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept]Ancient Tomes[/hyperlink] and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldGateLoreConcept]World Gate[/hyperlink], which act as magic portals through the Astral Sea.

GLOBAL.MagelocksLoreConcept.name: Magelock
GLOBAL.MagelocksLoreConcept.description:
Magelock weapons are magic-powered ranged weapons, derived from the ordnance created by mighty empires long since fallen. By fusing the arcane with the physical, Magelock mechanisms allow skilled marksmen to hit faraway targets with great impact and accuracy.

Magelock weaponry permeates all corners of the Astral Sea Lore, implying analogous origins on various realms, yet the remnants of the ruined Commonwealth Lore remain most infamous for wielding these terrible weapons.

GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept.name: Myrrida
GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept.description:
Many myths surround the fabled kingdom of Myrrida, where [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] once ruled the small races across the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink]. Undeniable is the wealth and grandeur, still exhibited within its ruined monumental structures and cities. Yet there is much debate among [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] about the fall of Myrrida. Some say the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] became corrupted by their power, giving rise to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept]Traitor Kings[/hyperlink]. Others blame [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archon[/hyperlink] suppression for the destruction of a lost utopia.

Certain is that the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and their allied [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Elder Dragons[/hyperlink] besieged Myrrida, ending the long Age of Giants and distantly presaging the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept]Endailon Crisis[/hyperlink]. While the various Giant Clans seek to carry on the legacy of their ancient forefathers, their deeds pale beside the marveled legends of Myrrida.

GLOBAL.ObbadothLoreConcept.name: Obbadoth
GLOBAL.ObbadothLoreConcept.description: Obbadoth is an infernal [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]World[/hyperlink] ruled by Demonic Princes, where fiends make the laws and sins are virtuous. Many realms of this world are affected by spells which enhance one's primal urges, which often leads to bloodshed, debauchery, and everything in between. Very few [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] can withstand Obbadoth's infernal influence.

GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept.name: Pantheon
GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept.description: With many [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Wizard Kings[/hyperlink] seeing themselves as living gods, it is no surprise their gathering at [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink] became known as the Pantheon. In this sanctuary the members of the Pantheon debate and scheme to alter the fate of the cosmos. The Pantheon consists of many factions and alliances, of which the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CovenantFactionLoreConcept]Covenant[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadraiFactionLoreConcept]Shad'rai[/hyperlink] are most prominent.

GLOBAL.PellariLoreConcept.name: Pellari
GLOBAL.PellariLoreConcept.description:
Not much is known about the Pellari, for reports from the Fey realm [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept]Duatha[/hyperlink] are scarce and notoriously unreliable. What has been accepted as common knowledge is that the Pellari are a diverse group of different animalistic races which are united by their display of almost excessive friendliness and a preference for simple, pastoral life.

Some sources pick up on the theory that [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept]Duatha[/hyperlink] is a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DreamersLoreConcept]Dreamer[/hyperlink] and propose that the Pellari are one of her childish creations; a proposition that often gets extended to the Fey themselves and their unique magic properties that seem to defy all arcane rules and reason.

GLOBAL.PrimalSpiritsLoreConcept.name: Primal Spirits
GLOBAL.PrimalSpiritsLoreConcept.description: Primal Spirits are spiritual representations of the many aspects of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NatureConcept]Nature[/hyperlink], worshiped by various peoples in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. Each Spirit brings its own doctrines on society, and followers look up to them for guidance throughout all aspects of life. There are many different beliefs surrounding these spirits, but they all have one thing in common: in battle their worshipers can call upon the powers of their chosen Spirit to empower and aid them. The most common Primal Spirits are the Sylvan Wolf, Ash Sabertooth, Mire Crocodile, Dune Serpent, Storm Crow, Glacial Mammoth, and Tunneling Spider.

GLOBAL.RevenantsLoreConcept.name: Revenants
GLOBAL.RevenantsLoreConcept.description: Once [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] in life, the soul-cursed Revenants invoke the greatest fear in the enemies of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink]. For their unlife represents the ultimate triumph of corruption, when not even the most virtuous souls may escape. First encountered on [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds[/hyperlink] locked through [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SealLoreConcept]Seals[/hyperlink], the Revenant curse has since then spread to many Necropolises which the Archons left behind in their cosmic wars.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfArtificingLoreConcept.name: School of Artificing
GLOBAL.SchoolOfArtificingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept]Horwynd[/hyperlink] School of Artificing diligently collect and preserve magical artifacts and monuments. When the Scholars of Shrouding proposed to cache the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir's[/hyperlink] secrets in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShroudedIsleConcept]Shrouded Isles[/hyperlink], the Scholars of Artificing drew on their expertise in magical structures to construct the Portals that connect these hidden Realms to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.SchoolOfShroudingLoreConcept.name: School of Shrouding
GLOBAL.SchoolOfShroudingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept]Horwynd[/hyperlink] School of Shrouding were conservators and archivists of secret knowledge found in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink]. When the development of experimental spells was repressed by the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink], the guileful Scholars of Shrouding suggested securing them in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShroudedIsleConcept]Shrouded Isles[/hyperlink], while also shrouding the Portals that lead to them.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfVitalizingLoreConcept.name: School of Vitalizing
GLOBAL.SchoolOfVitalizingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept]Horwynd[/hyperlink] School of Vitalizing were primarily conservators and breeders of flora and fauna. Once the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShroudedIsleConcept]Shrouded Isles[/hyperlink] were shaped, the Scholars of Vitalizing applied their knowledge of growth and life to create regenerating habitats, where the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir's[/hyperlink] sanctuaries remain untouched by the oppression of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.SchoolOfWardingLoreConcept.name: School of Warding
GLOBAL.SchoolOfWardingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept]Horwynd[/hyperlink] School of Warding were originally tasked with preserving knowledge of battle and war. When the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] established the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CircleOfDeogaiLoreConcept]Circles of Deogai[/hyperlink], the School of honorable warriors and knights deployed their holy power to protect the Portals to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShroudedIsleConcept]Shrouded Isles[/hyperlink] against invading forces and the inquisitive agents of the Archons.

GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept.name: Umbral Demons
GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept.description: The Umbral Demons, sometimes referred to as Shadow Demons, are molded by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink]. Their forbidden inception reputedly involves distorting corrupted souls into the shapes of the Umbral Demons. The tainted creatures feed on magic leaking from the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. They first consumed the world of their creation, until only the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept]Umbral Abyss[/hyperlink] remained: A twisted husk filled with blackness and despair. Since then, the Umbral Demons have preyed on many worlds, including [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AthlaLoreConcept]Athla[/hyperlink], allowing the Umbral Abyss to spread in their wake.

GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept.name: Umbral Abyss
GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept.description:
Beyond the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink] and even the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Void[/hyperlink] an eldritch infestation lurks: The Umbral Abyss, the dominion of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink]. Here is where [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept]Umbral Demons[/hyperlink] reign, molded through a vile corruption of the power of Creation itself. Vile and toxic to any living being, the Umbral Abyss ever seeks to corrupt the Astral Sea, tearing festering wounds into the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink]. The [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept]Gloomwatch[/hyperlink] fight back against the corruption, but wherever they wage war, the scars of battle that stain the realms never fully heal.

Through the Ages, the Umbral Abyss has claimed many civilizations, and their remnants of knowledge and treasure have lured many adventurers and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept]wizards[/hyperlink] to a fate many consider worse than death.

GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept.name: Torment of Shadows
GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept.description: In the darkness of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Astral Void[/hyperlink], the banished Wizards are tormented by visions and maddening voices. Survivors describe vastly different experiences, as if the cosmos creates a reckoning for a Wizard's individual actions and beliefs. Those that succumb are doomed to drift forever as a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept]Lost Wizards[/hyperlink], mad husks of which little remains other than their lust for power.

GLOBAL.ShadraiFactionLoreConcept.name: Shad'rai
GLOBAL.ShadraiFactionLoreConcept.description: A group of ambitious [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] who formed a volatile cabal in order to claim power within the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept]Pantheon[/hyperlink] and the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. They believe no power should be hidden from anyone and are known for their schemes and invasions of realms they deem worthy of their domination. Their chaotic tendencies often put them in direct opposition to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CovenantFactionLoreConcept]Covenant[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept.name: Souls
GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept.description:
Souls are the eternal Astral manifestations of all living beings. When someone dies, their soul is released to return to [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept]the Well of Creation[/hyperlink]. This journey through the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralFlowsLoreConcept]Astral Flows[/hyperlink] is arduous and many [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralDwellersLoreConcept]Astral Sea Dwellers[/hyperlink] hunt these souls. Especially troubled souls may find themselves lost or captured during the journey.

With specific magics, souls can be captured for nefarious purposes. Some dark races use souls as a valuable currency that allows the summoning of undead beings.

GLOBAL.StoneClanLoreConcept.name: Rock Clan
GLOBAL.StoneClanLoreConcept.description: Persistent and steady as stone, the Rock Clan has the patience to build what the other Giant Clans can only dream of conquering. They shun contact with the smaller races, going to great lengths to keep their dungeon halls, where faint echoes of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida’s splendor[/hyperlink] are recalled, inaccessible.

GLOBAL.StormClanLoreConcept.name: Storm Clan
GLOBAL.StormClanLoreConcept.description: First silent then tempestuous, the Storm Clan prefers to strike when it is the least expected. The leaders of this Giant Clan study the lost magic of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink], seeking to emulate the arcane powers of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] of old.

GLOBAL.SyronLoreConcept.name: Syrons
GLOBAL.SyronLoreConcept.description: Originally descendants of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept]Maer[/hyperlink], the first Syrons were a part of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept]Gloomwatch[/hyperlink] to protect the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DreamersLoreConcept]Dreamers[/hyperlink] from the corrupting influence of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept]Urrath[/hyperlink]. They settled on idyllic worlds where the light of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink]’s creation still burned bright, until the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept]Umbral Demons[/hyperlink] eventually invaded. Most of the Syrons were massacred and many of the survivors enslaved, their devoured home worlds overrun by the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept]Umbral Abyss[/hyperlink]. The few Syrons that escaped spread across the Astral Sea, but many found themselves locked in an endless crusade against the Umbral Demons, even if they formally abandoned the Gloomwatch long ago.

GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept.name: The Fracturing
GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept.description:
The Fracturing was the magical cataclysm that erased the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept]Unmakers[/hyperlink] from the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink] and brought an end to their experiments. The few stories that survived the calamity speak of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept]Fractures[/hyperlink] suddenly growing and erupting in a chain reaction.

Through the Fracturing, the affected worlds were changed forever. The land became barren, magic turned hazardous; some of their inhabitants adapted, and some were altered beyond recognition.

GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept.name: The Well
GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept.description: According to mythology, the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink] pulled the cosmos from the Well of Creation. All later creations of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink] would date back to this one wonder. From [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink], located deep in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink], the Well can be seen as a looming bright omen, a slowly swirling white maelstrom from which the light of creation emerges in shifting directions. All <<c:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept]Souls[/hyperlink]>> of the dead are drawn to return to the Well on their final journey.

GLOBAL.TidolonLoreConcept.name: Tidolon
GLOBAL.TidolonLoreConcept.description: Tidolon is known for its vast oceans and relatively low density of land. Islands and small continents dot the massive sea of blue. Many aquatic beings thrive on this [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]World[/hyperlink], and it is said many lost treasures and whole empires are hidden beneath its surface.

GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept.name: Tomes of Knowledge
GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept.description:
Tomes of power hold certain fundamental truths and secrets of the cosmos, often associated with specific [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinitiesLoreConcept]Affinities[/hyperlink]. These works are mystical manuscripts written by beings of power like [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink], to pass on their mastery of the subject within.

True mastery of a Tome can only be achieved through dedicated focus. Every stage of mastery will grant powers that can alter realms and even a Godir's subjects themselves.

GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept.name: Traitor Kings
GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept.description:
The Traitor Kings were the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] of old [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink] who broke allegiance to the Titans, ending the ancient agreement between Elder Giants and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink]. Drunk on the glory of their kingdom they rejected a faith centered on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink], proclaiming that the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] themselves had acted as gods and should therefore be worshiped as such.

Acting as ruthless overlords the Traitor Kings engaged in dark magic, twisting stolen knowledge from the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept]Eternal Council[/hyperlink] to achieve immortality. Yet when the war with the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Elder Dragons[/hyperlink] reached their thrones, they fell one by one, leaving only myths of their corrupt souls still haunting the ruins of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept.name: Unmakers
GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept.description:
The Unmakers were a group of ambitious wizards whose experiments devastated large sections of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink], now known as the Fractured Realms. They rose to power after the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept]Endailon Crisis[/hyperlink] had destroyed or weakened the dominant forces of previous ages. Believing themselves capable of unraveling the very essence of mana and magic, the Unmakers competed and cooperated among themselves, striving to recreate the powers flowing from the Well of Creation.

Among the nomadic tribes of the Fractured Worlds, countless cautionary tales speak of the Unmakers and their experiments: how they tore the fabrics of magic, scarred the realms with [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept]Fractures[/hyperlink] — and ultimately, as the moral of the story, perished in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept]the Fracturing[/hyperlink] that reshaped the realms.

GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept.name: Urrath
GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept.description: Urrath is the nemesis of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink] and widely believed to be the bringer of darkness and corruption to the cosmos. The most terrifying creatures known to exist, such as the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept]Astral Sea Monsters[/hyperlink], are blamed on Urrath's influence, as is all evil running through the veins of mortal races.

GLOBAL.UrwildernessLoreConcept.name: Urwilderness
GLOBAL.UrwildernessLoreConcept.description:
When the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Elder Dragons[/hyperlink] shaped the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds Within[/hyperlink], they aroused the great beasts dwelling in its raw primal shell. Calling upon the powers of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept]Nature Endailon[/hyperlink], these Primordial Beasts surrounded themselves in an overgrown Urwilderness, where creatures of many vicious, but also graceful, designs came to be and that even the Elder Dragons and Giants shunned.

Thus, when the small races arrived on the realms, their spreading settlements soon clashed with the enduring jungle of the Urwilderness. Enraged by the intrusions of civilization, the Primordial Beasts started to rampage across the realms, destroying everything in their wake.

Moved by the woes of the small races, the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept]Elder Giants[/hyperlink] rose to their defense, initiating the Great Hunt. Gifted with the celestial chains of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]Archons[/hyperlink], the Elder Giants thinned out the Urwilderness and bound the Primordial Beasts within mighty prisons. It was the dawn of the Age of Giants and thereupon the founding of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept]Myrrida[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ValleyofWondersLoreConcept.name: Valley of Wonders
GLOBAL.ValleyofWondersLoreConcept.description: The Valley of Wonders is a historic area on the Blessed Continent on the world of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AthlaLoreConcept]Athla[/hyperlink]. Once the home of the Elven Court of House Inioch, it has seen much turmoil since the first Athlan humans sacked the fabled court. It remains an area of great natural beauty and magical potency.

GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept.name: Wizard King
GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept.description: Wizard Kings are ancient archmages who seek power across the realms of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. Before joining the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept]Pantheon[/hyperlink] at [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept]Magehaven[/hyperlink], the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept]Torment of Shadows[/hyperlink] left many mentally warped. Wizard Kings are no longer limited to their original mortal form, and can create people vastly different from themselves.

GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept.name: Worlds Within
GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept.description:
The material worlds embedded within the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Astral Sea[/hyperlink]. They are the places where mortal races thrive and build their empires, and where the grand plots of the past and coming ages unfold.

According to ancient knowledge, the worlds were drawn from the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept]the Well[/hyperlink] by the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AllfatherLoreConcept]Allfather[/hyperlink], after which [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept]Dragons[/hyperlink] shaped them and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept]Giants[/hyperlink] refined them. Through the ages, the worlds and their distinguished realms have been altered and reshaped by various factions and forces, making each uniquely distinct in terms of the lay of the land, creatures and people living there, but also the abundance of magic and its representing [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinitiesLoreConcept]Affinities[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.WorldGateLoreConcept.name: World Gate
GLOBAL.WorldGateLoreConcept.description: To shortcut the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralFlowsLoreConcept]dangerous journey[/hyperlink] to other [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds[/hyperlink], the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept]Godir[/hyperlink] have devised elaborate portal structures known as World Gates, which allow the user to travel to other worlds almost instantly. Great knowledge and skill is required to use such a portal. Otherwise, the Godir and their companions may be lost in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept]Astral Void[/hyperlink] or stranded on an isolated world.

GLOBAL.SpellConcept.name: Spell
GLOBAL.SpellConcept.description:
Magical rites and incantations used by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LeaderConcept]Rulers[/hyperlink]. Obtained through [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ResearchConcept]Research[/hyperlink].

Spells usually cost [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapCastingPointConcept]World Map Casting Points[/hyperlink] or [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatCastingPointConcept]Combat Casting Points[/hyperlink].

Spells are divided in 2 main categories, depending on where they can be cast. Each category has their own collection of spell types:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapSpellConcept]World Map Spells[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatSpellConcept]Combat Spells[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.ClassicTurnConcept.name: Classic Turns
GLOBAL.ClassicTurnConcept.description: In classic turns, everyone plays their turn in the order of the Rulers list. Once the last Ruler has ended their turn, the next round will start with the first Ruler.

GLOBAL.SimultaneousTurnConcept.name: Simultaneous Turns
GLOBAL.SimultaneousTurnConcept.description: In simultaneous turns, everyone plays their turn at the same time. Once each Ruler has ended their turn, the next round will start.

GLOBAL.ClaimConcept.name: Claim
GLOBAL.ClaimConcept.description:
Province Claims indicate the intention of owning a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Province[/hyperlink].

They appear on [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink] adjacent to:A [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.OutpostConcept]Outposts[/hyperlink]Explored [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept]Ancient Wonders[/hyperlink]
If other [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LeaderConcept]Rulers[/hyperlink] build on claimed provinces, the Rulers will meet and have a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CasusBelliConcept]Grievance[/hyperlink] against them. Building on a province claimed by a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free City[/hyperlink] will incur a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityRelationConcept]Relations[/hyperlink] penalty.

Rulers also have distant claims on provinces up to a distance of 3 away from their owned domain. Distant claims yield less severe penalties and are only violated by building an outpost or exploring an Ancient Wonder.

GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept.name: Production
GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept.description:
Production is used for building [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].

Every [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turn[/hyperlink], Production is spent on the first structure in the City's [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProductionQueueConcept]Production Queue[/hyperlink]. Leftover Production becomes [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SurplusConcept]Surplus[/hyperlink].

Gain Production by:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceAnnexationConcept]Annexing[/hyperlink] Iron Deposits.Building Foresters and Quarries in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink].Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].Collecting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.FoodConcept.name: Food
GLOBAL.FoodConcept.description:
Food is used to gain new [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PopulationConcept]Population[/hyperlink] in your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink] and pay [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PopulationUpkeepConcept]Population Upkeep[/hyperlink]. Greater Food income will cause Cities to grow faster.

Gain Food by:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceAnnexationConcept]Annexing[/hyperlink] Pastures.Building Farms and Foresters in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink].Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].Collecting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink].A city with insufficient food income will suffer from [hyperlink,GLOBAL.StarvationConcept]Starvation[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ProductionConcept.name: Production
GLOBAL.ProductionConcept.description:
Production is used in City as the base value for both Unit Production and Structure Production, enabling cities to produce items faster.

Gain Production by:Annexing Iron Deposits.Building Foresters and Quarries in Province.

GLOBAL.RecruitmentPointsConcept.name: Recruitment Points
GLOBAL.RecruitmentPointsConcept.description: Recruitment points are used in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.RequestMilitaryAidConcept]Rally of the Lieges[/hyperlink] to draft [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink] into your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] or to send them to aid in the defense of vassal houses. Recruitment points are primarily gained from [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityRelationConcept]Relations[/hyperlink] with <minorcity></minorcity> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free Cities[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.UnitProductionConcept.name: Draft
GLOBAL.UnitProductionConcept.description:
Draft is used for recruiting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink] in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink].

Spent on the first Unit in the City's Unit [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProductionQueueConcept]Production Queue[/hyperlink] every [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turn[/hyperlink]. Leftover Draft becomes [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SurplusConcept]Surplus[/hyperlink].

Gain Draft by:Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.BindingEssenceConcept.name: Binding Essence and Fragments
GLOBAL.BindingEssenceConcept.description:
Binding Essence and Fragments are the remains of magical items.

They are used for crafting custom items in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ItemForgeConcept]Item Forge[/hyperlink].
Crafting Tier 3 or 4 items costs Binding Fragments in addition to the Binding Essence cost.

Binding Essence is gained by disenchanting any items in the arsenal.
Binding Fragments are gained by disenchanting Tier 3 or 4 items in the arsenal.

GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept.name: Whispering Stone
GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept.description:
Whispering Stones are given to a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free City[/hyperlink] to begin [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NegotiationConcept]Negotiations[/hyperlink], which can lead to it becoming your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PactOfVassalageConcept]Vassal[/hyperlink]. Having more allows you to befriend multiple [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free Cities[/hyperlink] at once.

Unused Whispering Stones can be given to your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink] to gain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStabilityConcept]City Stability[/hyperlink].

Gain more Whispering Stones via [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept]Empire Development[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.GoldConcept.name: Gold
GLOBAL.GoldConcept.description:
Gold is your material wealth and riches. Used for:Recruiting new [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink].Paying [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitUpkeepConcept]Unit Upkeep[/hyperlink].Building [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].
Gain Gold by:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceAnnexationConcept]Annexing[/hyperlink] Gold Veins.Building Mines in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink].Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].Collecting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept.name: Imperium
GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept.description:
Imperium represents your authority and reputation in the mortal realm.

Used for:Founding [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink] from [hyperlink,GLOBAL.OutpostConcept]Outposts[/hyperlink].Taking over conquered [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink].Buying Empire Skills.Gain Imperium by developing the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WizardTowerConcept]Wizard Tower[/hyperlink] in your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ThroneCityConcept]Throne City[/hyperlink] and by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceAnnexationConcept]annexing[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept]Ancient Wonders[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.InfluenceConcept.name: Whispering Stone Strength
GLOBAL.InfluenceConcept.description: <whisperingStone></whisperingStone> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept]Whispering Stones[/hyperlink] have a certain <allegiance></allegiance> strength that determines how effective they are at manipulating <minorcity></minorcity> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free Cities[/hyperlink]. During [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NegotiationConcept]Negotiations[/hyperlink], <whisperingStone></whisperingStone> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept]Whispering Stones[/hyperlink] generate allegiance based on their strength. The higher the strength, the sooner the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NegotiationConcept]Negotiations[/hyperlink] will succeed.

GLOBAL.KnowledgeConcept.name: Knowledge
GLOBAL.KnowledgeConcept.description:
Knowledge is the collective arcane wisdom of your sages and wise men, as they explore the secrets of the magical [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinityConcept]Affinities[/hyperlink].

Used for researching [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpellConcept]Spells[/hyperlink] and other skills from [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeConcept]Tomes[/hyperlink].
Unlocking a tome increases the knowledge cost of all skills in future tomes.

If there is no active research, then leftover Knowledge will be kept as [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SurplusConcept]Surplus[/hyperlink].

Gain Knowledge by:Building Research Posts in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink].Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].Collecting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ManaConcept.name: Mana
GLOBAL.ManaConcept.description: <mana></mana> Mana is the raw source of magic. Used for:<bulletlist><bullet>Casting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpellConcept]Spells[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Summoning magical [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Paying [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitUpkeepConcept]Unit Upkeep[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>Gain <mana></mana> Mana by:<bulletlist><bullet>[hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceAnnexationConcept]Annexing[/hyperlink] Mana Nodes.</bullet><bullet>Building Conduits in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Collecting [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept.name: Ancient Wonder
GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept.description:
An Ancient Wonder is a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Location[/hyperlink] that contains adventure and rewards. It can only be explored by a single [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArmyConcept]Army[/hyperlink] led by a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HeroConcept]Hero[/hyperlink].

When cleared, it can be annexed by a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink]. When annexed it will provide [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept]City Income[/hyperlink] and special [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink] in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.RequestMilitaryAidConcept]Rally of the Lieges[/hyperlink]. An annexed Ancient Wonder counts as a type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink].

Ancient Wonders can be Bronze, Silver, or Gold, depending on rarity, difficulty and value.

GLOBAL.CityCenterConcept.name: City Center
GLOBAL.CityCenterConcept.description: The [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Location[/hyperlink] on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink] which lies at the origin of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] Domain.

GLOBAL.CityTierConcept.name: City Tier
GLOBAL.CityTierConcept.description: [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] Tier is determined by its last completed Town Hall [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structure[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ConduitConcept.name: Conduit
GLOBAL.ConduitConcept.description: A Conduit is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.DomainConcept.name: Domain
GLOBAL.DomainConcept.description: The collection of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink] belonging to the city. The Ruler will have a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ClaimConcept]Claim[/hyperlink] on provinces adjacent to their city domain. Friendly units have to spend 2 less <movementgeneral></movementgeneral> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MovePointConcept]Move Points[/hyperlink] to traverse terrain in friendly domains.

GLOBAL.FarmConcept.name: Farm
GLOBAL.FarmConcept.description: A Farm is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <food></food> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FoodConcept]Food[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.FisheryConcept.name: Fishery
GLOBAL.FisheryConcept.description: A Fishery is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <food></food> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FoodConcept]Food[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.ForesterConcept.name: Forester
GLOBAL.ForesterConcept.description: A Forester is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <food></food> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FoodConcept]Food[/hyperlink] and <structureprod></structureprod> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept]Production[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.GuildSlotConcept.name: Guild Slot
GLOBAL.GuildSlotConcept.description:
Represents a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City's[/hyperlink] capacity for powerful economic [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink] called Guilds.

Typically a city will only have a single Guild Slot.

GLOBAL.InfestationConcept.name: Infestation
GLOBAL.InfestationConcept.description:
Areas under the control of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MarauderConcept]Marauders[/hyperlink], who increase in numbers and over time take over adjacent [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink]. They will periodically send forth raiding parties that can potentially start a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink] on a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] without needing a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HeroConcept]Hero[/hyperlink].

Destroying the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept]Infestation Spawner[/hyperlink] will clear the infestation and grant the destroyer great rewards based on tier and size of the Infestation.

When an Infestation grows into one of your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Provinces[/hyperlink], it will continuously [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PillagingConcept]pillage[/hyperlink] its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] until the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept]Infestation Spawner[/hyperlink] is destroyed.

Infestations have several states, its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept]Infestation Spawner[/hyperlink] will indicate its current state, and each state will take several [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turns[/hyperlink] to activate: Deep Sleep/Sleeping/Awakening. The infestation will become active. Patrolling. The infestation will patrol its domain. Invasion. A raiding party will emerge. Recovering. The infestation will reinforce its patrolling armies.Infestations can be [hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationNeutralityConcept]Neutral[/hyperlink] to certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empires[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.InfestationNeutralityConcept.name: Infestation Neutrality
GLOBAL.InfestationNeutralityConcept.description:
[hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationConcept]Infestations[/hyperlink] are hostile to all [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empires[/hyperlink] by default, but they can become neutral to one or more Empires in certain circumstances.

While neutral to an Empire:The Infestation's armies will never attack the Empire.The Infestation will not pillage the Empire's Province Improvements.The Infestation will not send out raiding parties to the Empire.The Infestation can still grow into the Empire's domain.If the Empire attacks the Infestation's armies, the Infestation stops being neutral towards the Empire.Infestations summoned by an Empire always start out neutral towards them.

GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept.name: Infestation Spawner
GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept.description: An Infestation Spawner is a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Location[/hyperlink] that causes an [hyperlink,GLOBAL.InfestationConcept]Infestation[/hyperlink] to take place.

GLOBAL.LocationConcept.name: Location
GLOBAL.LocationConcept.description:
A special building or site on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink], such as a watchtower, gold vein or bandit lair.
Guarded locations can be conquered to earn rewards.Take ownership of a location by moving [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink] onto to it.Many locations give [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ResourceConcept]Resources[/hyperlink] when within a city's domain.

GLOBAL.MagicMaterialConcept.name: Magic Materials
GLOBAL.MagicMaterialConcept.description:
Magic Materials are [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NodeConcept]Resource Nodes[/hyperlink] that provide bonus effects to your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink], as well as provide [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept]City Income[/hyperlink]. These bonus effects can be traded to other [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empires[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free Cities[/hyperlink].

If all Magic Materials of the type are collected, they will provide an additional powerful bonus. The following bonuses are available:

[hyperlink,GLOBAL.TOKENSETBONUS.IMPERIAL_ESSENCE]Imperial Essence[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.TOKENSETBONUS.COSMICFLUX_ELIXIR]Cosmoflux Elixir[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.TOKENSETBONUS.RINGS_OF_BINDING]Rings of Binding[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.MineConcept.name: Mine
GLOBAL.MineConcept.description: A Mine is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <gold></gold> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GoldConcept]Gold[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.NodeConcept.name: Node
GLOBAL.NodeConcept.description: Nodes are [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Locations[/hyperlink] on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink] which grant bonus income when the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Province[/hyperlink] they are located in is annexed to a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.PickupConcept.name: Pickup
GLOBAL.PickupConcept.description:
One-time [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ResourceConcept]Resource[/hyperlink] packs on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink]. Their rewards can be acquired by moving an [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArmyConcept]Army[/hyperlink] onto them.

A Pickup is removed once its rewards are collected.

GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept.name: Province Improvement
GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept.description:
Structures that a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] builds in a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Province[/hyperlink] to add that province to its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].

Different improvements are available in a province depending on what [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceFeatureConcept]Province Features[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Locations[/hyperlink] are within it.

A city can support one improvement for each [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PopulationConcept]Population[/hyperlink] it has after the first one.

GLOBAL.QuarryConcept.name: Quarry
GLOBAL.QuarryConcept.description: A Quarry is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <structureprod></structureprod> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept]Production[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.ResearchPostConcept.name: Research Post
GLOBAL.ResearchPostConcept.description: A Research Post is a base [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvement[/hyperlink] with the following benefits:<bulletlist><bullet>Provides <knowledge></knowledge> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.KnowledgeConcept]Knowledge[/hyperlink] income.</bullet><bullet>Meeting the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BoostConcept]Boost[/hyperlink] requirement for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Adjacency bonuses of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpecialImprovementConcept]Special Province Improvements[/hyperlink].</bullet><bullet>Bonuses that scale over specific province improvement types in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.RootNodeConcept.name: Root Node
GLOBAL.RootNodeConcept.description: Node required to achieve Magic Victory. Base Root Nodes provide Mana and can be converted to a different Affinity for additional City Income.

GLOBAL.RuinedNodeConcept.name: Ruined Node
GLOBAL.RuinedNodeConcept.description: Ruined Nodes are [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NodeConcept]Resource Nodes[/hyperlink] that have been depleted by overharvesting or other means.<bulletlist><bullet>Ruined Nodes no longer provide any income or bonuses.</bullet><bullet>Ruined Nodes still grant the option of building certain [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvements[/hyperlink] in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceConcept]Province[/hyperlink] their intact versions would allow.</bullet><bullet>Ruined Nodes can be restored as long as you have claimed them, restoring them costs <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink].<bulletlist><bullet>This cost is decreased each <turn></turn> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turn[/hyperlink] the Ruined Node exists, until a minimum cost is reached.</bullet><bullet>When restored, Ruined Nodes are replaced by their intact versions which provide their income and bonuses again.</bullet></bulletlist></bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.WizardTowerConcept.name: Wizard Tower
GLOBAL.WizardTowerConcept.description:
The Wizard Tower is the center of a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LeaderConcept]Ruler[/hyperlink]'s powers. Only one can be built in the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ThroneCityConcept]Throne City[/hyperlink] after building the Town Hall II .

It unlocks Empire-wide benefits, provides [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept]Imperium[/hyperlink] income, and improves the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.VisionRangeConcept]Vision Range[/hyperlink] of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ThroneCityConcept]Throne City[/hyperlink].

Allows the construction of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ItemForgeConcept]Item Forge[/hyperlink] after building the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.STRUCTURE_UPGRADES.WIZARD_TOWER_FOUNDATION]Wizard Tower: Foundation[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.AbsorbingConcept.name: Absorbing
GLOBAL.AbsorbingConcept.description: Absorbing a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] makes it part of your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] under your direct control, retaining its original race and culture.

GLOBAL.AdvisorConcept.name: Advisor
GLOBAL.AdvisorConcept.description:
The Advisor shows new tutorial and advice messages. Advice messages contain tips about the current situation of your empire.

It can be accessed through the ? banner located near the bottom right of the screen.

GLOBAL.AffinityConcept.name: Affinity
GLOBAL.AffinityConcept.description:
The Affinity of an [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] is an indication of its strengths, specializations, and available [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeConcept]Tomes[/hyperlink].

The Affinity types are: [hyperlink,GLOBAL.OrderConcept]Order Affinity[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ChaosConcept]Chaos Affinity[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.NatureConcept]Nature Affinity[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.MateriumConcept]Materium Affinity[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralConcept]Astral Affinity[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ShadowConcept]Shadow Affinity[/hyperlink]
Starting Affinity points are determined by faction creation choices. Affinity points are obtained by selecting the respective [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeConcept]Tomes[/hyperlink] during [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ResearchConcept]Research[/hyperlink].

Having more Affinity points will increase the rate at which you unlock new [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept]Empire Skills[/hyperlink] in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept]Empire Development[/hyperlink].

To unlock higher tier [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TomeConcept]Tomes[/hyperlink], you will need to have a certain amount of Affinity points that match with the Affinity of those tomes.

GLOBAL.ArmyConcept.name: Army
GLOBAL.ArmyConcept.description:
An army is a collection of maximum 6 [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Units[/hyperlink].

Armies can be moved on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink], explore [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LocationConcept]Locations[/hyperlink], collect [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink], and engage in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.ArtifactConcept.name: Artifact
GLOBAL.ArtifactConcept.description:
Artifacts are unique items bound to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] of a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PlayerConcept]Player[/hyperlink]. They provide unique bonuses to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] controlling them.
Artifacts are often part of a collection. Completing the collection will trigger an impactful Collection Happening.Artifacts may be traded between [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PlayerConcept]Players[/hyperlink].When defeating a player, all Artifacts of that player are claimed by the defeating player.

GLOBAL.AstralEchoesConcept.name: Astral Echoes
GLOBAL.AstralEchoesConcept.description:
Astral Echoes are special resources gained through:
Astral Echoes [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PickupConcept]Pickups[/hyperlink], only visible to and collectible by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.LeaderConcept]Rulers[/hyperlink] of certain Mystic Subcultures.

This resource is used for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EchoCastingConcept]Echo Casting[/hyperlink] by the Mystic School of Attunement.

This resource is used for [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EchoInfusionConcept]Echo Infusion[/hyperlink] by the Mystic School of Summoning.

GLOBAL.BoostConcept.name: Boost
GLOBAL.BoostConcept.description:
Boosting a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structure[/hyperlink] reduces its cost by 30%.

Boosts automatically apply when the requirements are met.

GLOBAL.BuffDebuffSpellConcept.name: Buff/Debuff Spell
GLOBAL.BuffDebuffSpellConcept.description: <bulletlist><bullet>Buffs allies and debuffs enemies in battle.</bullet><bullet>Costs <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] and <optactical></optactical> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatCastingPointConcept]Combat Casting Points[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.HealingBuffSpellConcept.name: Buff/Healing Spell
GLOBAL.HealingBuffSpellConcept.description: <bulletlist><bullet>Heals and buffs allies in battle.</bullet><bullet>Costs <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] and <optactical></optactical> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatCastingPointConcept]Combat Casting Points[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.BuffSpellConcept.name: Buff Spell
GLOBAL.BuffSpellConcept.description: <bulletlist><bullet>Buffs allies in battle.</bullet><bullet>Costs <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] and <optactical></optactical> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatCastingPointConcept]Combat Casting Points[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.CapturedConcept.name: Captured
GLOBAL.CapturedConcept.description: Captured units may be recruited after combat by spending <warspoils></warspoils> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WarSpoilsConcept]War Spoils[/hyperlink] or <gold></gold> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GoldConcept]Gold[/hyperlink] for non-Reaver empires.

GLOBAL.CastingLimitConcept.name: Casting Limit
GLOBAL.CastingLimitConcept.description: Casting Limit controls how many World Map Spell the user can cast in a single turn on the World Map. Casting Limit can be increased by building the S T R U C T U R E_ U P G R A D E S. C H A N N E L I N G C H A M B E R in your Throne City.

GLOBAL.ChaosConcept.name: Chaos Affinity
GLOBAL.ChaosConcept.description:
Chaos [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinityConcept]Affinity[/hyperlink] is the cosmic power of change and destruction. Associated with conquest, strife, and demonic forces.

Chaos Affinity is opposed by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.OrderConcept]Order Affinity[/hyperlink]. [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empires[/hyperlink] or [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free Cities[/hyperlink] with opposing affinities will suffer relation penalties.

GLOBAL.CityBattlementStructureConcept.name: Battlement Structure
GLOBAL.CityBattlementStructureConcept.description:
Battlement Structures are a type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept]City Defense Structure[/hyperlink] which spawns Battlement obstacles directly behind the walls in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink] during a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink].

Battlement obstacles provide buffs for units standing inside them.

When multiple Battlement Structures are built, only the most powerful Battlement obstacles will be present in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CityCapConcept.name: City Cap
GLOBAL.CityCapConcept.description:
The number of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink] your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] can control.

Exceeding your City Cap results in -25% [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept]City Income[/hyperlink] to all your [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]Cities[/hyperlink] for each [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] above City Cap.

Your City Cap can be increased through [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept]Empire Development[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept.name: City Defense Structure
GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept.description:
City Defense Structures are [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink] that typically grant [hyperlink,GLOBAL.FortificationHealthConcept]Fortification Health[/hyperlink] and provide defensive benefits in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink] during a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink].

There are different types of Defense Structures:[hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityWallStructureConcept]Wall Structures[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityTowerStructureConcept]Tower Structures[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.CitySupportStructureConcept]Support Structures[/hyperlink][hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityBattlementStructureConcept]Battlement Structures[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.CityConcept.name: City
GLOBAL.CityConcept.description:
Cities are located on the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapConcept]World Map[/hyperlink]. Cities are built by upgrading an [hyperlink,GLOBAL.OutpostConcept]Outpost[/hyperlink] or conquered through [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WarConcept]War[/hyperlink].

A city may either belong to an [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireConcept]Empire[/hyperlink] or be a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.IndependentCityConcept]Free City[/hyperlink].

The [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DomainConcept]Domain[/hyperlink] of a city expands according to its [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PopulationConcept]Population[/hyperlink]. Cities provide [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept]City Income[/hyperlink], which can be improved by adding [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept]City Structures[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept]Province Improvements[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept.name: City Income
GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept.description: City Income is the amount of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ResourceConcept]Resources[/hyperlink] a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] generates each <turn></turn> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turn[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CityRuinConcept.name: City Ruins
GLOBAL.CityRuinConcept.description: Remnants of a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink]. Can be rebuilt into a city for a cost.

GLOBAL.CitySpellConcept.name: City Spell
GLOBAL.CitySpellConcept.description: <bulletlist><bullet>Can affect the targeted city and its domain.</bullet><bullet>Costs <mana></mana> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ManaConcept]Mana[/hyperlink] and <caststrategic></caststrategic> [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldMapCastingPointConcept]World Map Casting Points[/hyperlink].</bullet></bulletlist>

GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept.name: City Structure
GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept.description:
City Structures provide economic bonuses for the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] they are built in.

They usually cost [hyperlink,GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept]Production[/hyperlink] and [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GoldConcept]Gold[/hyperlink], and are built using the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.StructureQueueConcept]Structure Queue[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CitySupportStructureConcept.name: Support Structure
GLOBAL.CitySupportStructureConcept.description:
Support Structures are a type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept]City Defense Structure[/hyperlink] which adds [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept]Combat Enchantments[/hyperlink] to the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink] in a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink].

These [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept]Combat Enchantments[/hyperlink] add tactical benefits to the Defender in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink].

Multiple Support Structures can be built and active in one [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CityTowerStructureConcept.name: Tower Structure
GLOBAL.CityTowerStructureConcept.description:
Tower Structures are a type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept]City Defense Structure[/hyperlink] which spawns Tower units in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink] during a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink].
Tower units are typically long range units that cannot move and act automatically.

When multiple Tower Structures are built, only the most powerful Tower units will be present in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CityWallStructureConcept.name: Wall Structure
GLOBAL.CityWallStructureConcept.description:
Wall Structures are a type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept]City Defense Structure[/hyperlink] which adds the requirement to [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink] the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CityConcept]City[/hyperlink] before hostile armies can attack.

They also define the Wall obstacles present in [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink] during a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SiegeConcept]Siege[/hyperlink].

When multiple Wall Structures are present, only the strongest Wall obstacle is present in combat.

GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept.name: Combat Enchantment
GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept.description:
A type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpellConcept]Spell[/hyperlink] that affects the entire battlefield.

While active, the spell triggers an effect at the start of the caster's [hyperlink,GLOBAL.TurnConcept]Turn[/hyperlink].

GLOBAL.CombatSpellConcept.name: Combat Spell
GLOBAL.CombatSpellConcept.description:
These are [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpellConcept]Spells[/hyperlink] that are cast during [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink], using [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatCastingPointConcept]Combat Casting Points[/hyperlink].

Types of Combat Spells are: [hyperlink,GLOBAL.BuffSpellConcept]Buff Spell[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept]Combat Enchantment[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatSummonSpellConcept]Combat Summon Spell[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DamageSpellConcept]Damage Spell[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.DebuffSpellConcept]Debuff Spell[/hyperlink] [hyperlink,GLOBAL.HealingSpellConcept]Healing Spell[/hyperlink]

GLOBAL.CombatSummonSpellConcept.name: Combat Summon Spell
GLOBAL.CombatSummonSpellConcept.description:
A type of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.SpellConcept]Spell[/hyperlink] that summons a [hyperlink,GLOBAL.UnitConcept]Unit[/hyperlink] with [hyperlink,GLOBAL.PROPERTIES.MAGIC_ORIGIN]Magic Origin[/hyperlink] onto any hex during [hyperlink,GLOBAL.CombatConcept]Combat[/hyperlink].

Units summoned in this way die when combat ends.

GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept.name: Empire Development
GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept.description:
Contains [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept]Empire Skills[/hyperlink] that can improve your empire's economy and unlock important abilities such as Seafaring and Tunneling.

[hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept]Empire Skills[/hyperlink] become available when enough Affinity Progress has been attained towards that particular [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinityConcept]Affinity[/hyperlink]. Available [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept]Empire Skills[/hyperlink] can be unlocked at any time by paying their [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept]Imperium[/hyperlink] cost.

GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept.name: Empire Skill
GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept.description:
Unlocks Empire-wide bonuses or grants powerful one-off rewards. Acquired via [hyperlink,GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept]Empire Development[/hyperlink].

Empire Skills require certain levels of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AffinityConcept]Affinity[/hyperlink] to unlock.

GLOBAL.ItemTransportationConcept.name: Item Transportation
GLOBAL.ItemTransportationConcept.description:
An item goes into transportation when you unequip it. When an item is being transported, it is unavailable for all heroes.

While in transport the item: Doesn't count towards arsenal effects.Can not be disenchanted.Can not be equipped.Can not be traded with other rulers.

GLOBAL.SpeedMarchConcept.name: Forced March
GLOBAL.SpeedMarchConcept.description:
